drafted_from: the six kits of tools/formulas (filter-rows-by-rules, evaluate-a-formula, list-comparisons, classify-a-record, read-a-fields-history, work-out-history-values) and tool-rows.json, read on origin/main bb8022539c
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep the rows of my list that are not Lost and have a value over 1000, and label each one big or other", with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"}."
no_lists_because: It names no list you must already have: the list you name is read from your own store, in whatever form it keeps its rows.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:find-and-classify-rows-by-rules" with store, the list, the rule tree, an optional formula and the labels.
3. Every attempt in the prove step must come out as it says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run reads the list's rows through the store and answers the kept rows, the labels and the rules left out.

worked_examples.title: Rows over a value and not Lost
worked_examples.ask: Keep the rows that are not Lost and have a value over 1000, and label each big or other.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The list deals holds r1 (Negotiation, 5000), r2 (Won, null) and r3 (Lost, 300).
worked_examples.hands_back: kept ["r1"], labels {"r1": "big"}, incomplete [], error_rows 0; r2 is not kept because its value is unknown.

worked_examples.title: A rule that names no field
worked_examples.ask: Keep the rows where the colour is red.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The list deals has no colour field.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept [], incomplete ["colour is not a field of deals"].
